newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-CASIRAGHI AND INCE MEET AGAIN AFTER ENGLAND DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CASIRAGHI AND INCE MEET AGAIN AFTER ENGLAND DEFEAT.

text.p: Italian Pierluigi Casiraghi and Englishman Paul Ince, two protagonists in Italy's 1-0 World Cup qualifying win over England at Wembley, renew their rivalry on Sunday when their clubs Lazio and Internazionale clash at the Olympic Stadium in Rome.
One-time league leaders Inter have faltered in recent months, taking only 13 points from 11 games since mid-November to drop to fifth place, seven points behind leaders Juventus.
On their last three outings, Inter have been beaten 2-0 by Bologna and had draws against Udinese and Perugia, prompting protests by fans about the club's English coach Roy Hodgson.
Club owner Massimo Moratti said: "We've got the players, it's the way that they play that has to improve and to do that we're going to have to train harder and show more determination."

Injury may rule out Inter's Dutch midfielder Aron Winter and striker Marco Branca while Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano's fitness is also doubtful following his efforts in Chile's 1-1 World Cup draw with Bolivia on Wednesday.
In their absence, Swiss international Ciriaco Sforza, Argentine Javier Zanetti and Salvatore Fresi join Ince in midfield with Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff partnered by Maurizio Ganz in attack.
Lazio come into the game just three weeks after replacing Czech coach Zdenek Zeman with Italy's 1982 World Cup winning captain Dino Zoff.
Zeman's sacking came at the end of a disappointing run which has seen Lazio sink to 11th place, 11 points behind Juventus, and go out of both the UEFA and Italian Cups.

So far Lazio have won their only game under Zoff, beating Udinese 3-2 in Udine two weeks ago when the side abandoned the attack-oriented 4-3-3 line-up favoured by Zeman for a more traditional 4-4-2 format.

Against Inter, Zoff will again field a four-man mifield comprising Giorgio Venturin, Australian Paul Okon, Czech Pavel Nedved and Diego Fuser with captain Guiseppe Signori partnering Casiraghi in attack.
Nedved, scorer of six league and cup goals this season, hopes to take advantage of the four-man midfield to get forward into a goalscoring position.
"Zoff has told me to get forward and make the most of my shooting skills," he said.
"With Okon and Venturin alongside me, I can push forward much more because I know there's always somebody there covering me."
